title: AI Lookbook Photos for New Collections | AIVideosUGC
description: Create AI lookbook photos for a new collection, with your outfits on a model in sunlit, editorial settings. Upload each outfit and build your launch looks.
h1: AI Lookbook Photos with an Editorial Feel
lead: AI lookbook photos put your outfits in a magazine-style setting, like a sunlit stone archway by the sea, so you can build a lookbook for a new drop one look at a time.
intro: In the example, a relaxed sand-colored suit with wide-leg trousers stands against pale stone arches with a glimpse of the sea. The light is warm, the pose is easy, and the setting supports the outfit instead of competing with it.

A lookbook sets the mood for a collection in a way plain product shots don't. Use it to announce a seasonal drop on Instagram, open a launch email with a few outfit ideas, or give stockists a feel for the season ahead.
tip: Upload each outfit as a full flat lay, top and bottom together, and choose one location for the whole collection so the images feel like one story.

steps.d: Photograph every piece of the look together, including shoes if they're part of what you sell.
Describe the place, light, and attitude, such as "stone archway by the sea, late afternoon sun, relaxed stance."
Download each look, then repeat with the next outfit in the same location so the set holds together.

ideas.d: Post five or six looks as an Instagram carousel on the day a collection goes live.
Try the same outfit on a city street and on a seaside terrace to find the setting that matches your brand.
Style linen suits and slip dresses for summer weddings and garden parties.

faq.q: Can I make a whole lookbook at once?
faq.a: Each run makes one photo, so you build a lookbook look by look. Keeping the setting the same in every description helps the photos feel like one shoot.

faq.q: Will the clothes in the photo match my real pieces?
faq.a: The cut, color, and fabric follow your upload, but small details like buttons and stitching can change. Look over each image next to the real garment before you publish it.

faq.q: What size are the lookbook photos?
faq.a: Square by default, which suits Instagram feed posts and carousels. Ask for some space around the outfit in your description if you plan to crop later.

faq.q: What photo format works for an AI lookbook?
faq.a: Lookbook photos are square by default, and the photo tool does not offer another ratio. Place a square image on a 9:16 canvas in your design tool for a Story layout.

overview.h2: Turn a Collection Into a Visual Story
overview.p: A lookbook frame does more than show a garment. It gives a launch a setting, pace, and point of view, so shoppers can understand how separate pieces belong together. Build each source as a complete outfit and repeat the visual language across the collection.

items.d: Lay out top, bottom, outer layer, shoes, and the accessory you intend to show together.
Photograph each piece flat and separated enough that a print, collar, or hem is not hidden by another garment.
Name the architecture, landscape, time of day, and attitude that can work for the next several looks.
Ask for relaxed standing, walking, or leaning rather than a pose that obscures the outfit.

results.h2: What a Lookbook Set Can Do

items.d: Give the outfit room to read from shoulder to shoe in one editorial frame.
Use styling and location to suggest how a collection works as a wardrobe.
Arrange several images for a carousel, email, or collection page.
Download the square image for commercial campaigns after checking the garments and scene.

scene_recipes.h2: Editorial Directions for a Seasonal Drop

items.d: Linen suit and sandals against pale stone arches with a glimpse of sea and warm late-afternoon light.
Coat, knit, and wide-leg trousers on a quiet concrete street after rain, with the full footwear visible.
Slip dress and lightweight jacket beside a garden path with soft daylight and a relaxed stance.
Sweater, denim, and crossbody bag in a bright cafe corner with a consistent neutral palette.

after_download.h2: Edit the Story Before You Share It

items.d: Make sure every featured piece matches the stock you can ship and the product names you publish.
Open with the hero look, then alternate silhouettes or color families so the carousel has rhythm.
Place dates, prices, product names, and collection links in the email or design tool after download.

good: Seasonal fashion drops with complete outfits
Editorial launches for apparel and accessories
Small catalogs that can share one location
not_ideal: A single item that needs a technical product shot
Outfits whose exact print alignment must be proven
A collection without enough source detail to identify each piece
